l.i: Miti Lumine cernat, Placatusque labores Tandem tollat amaros, Tristis flebit ocellus, Luctum pectora tollent, Amissque Syonis Plangent vsque puellas. Me quum Marte petuit Iniusto ferus hostis. O quàm terribilis ruit. Sic venator adurgens Ceruos figere tendit. Sic captare volucres Sueuit retibus auceps. Me crudelis acerbo Claudit carceris antro: Cuius desuper ora Saxum contegit ingens. Quum tam dira pauentem Vrgerent mala : vasto Quum iam gurgite feruens Pressum mergeret vnda: Iam me vita relinquet (Dixi) fracta, fluentes Iam vanescet in auras.

page.notes: The verse lines run together in one paragraph because the lines are not separated into stanzas on the scan; the printed line breaks are lost in this transcription. The faint mirrored text on the right side of the page is show-through from the reverse and is left out. Line 1 "Miti" has a swash capital M and may be read as "Mitis" in the printed original; I could not confirm the final letter, so it is given as read. The swash initials Q (Quum) and M (Me) are transcribed as their plain letters.
